newsitem.title: USA: USDA team to assess EU poultry packing plants.
newsitem.headline: USDA team to assess EU poultry packing plants.

text.p: A team from U.S. Agriculture Department will go to Europe to assess EU's poultry slaughter methods, the top agriculture policymakers for the United States and European Union said Monday.

Transatlantic poultry trade has been stalled for the past several weeks because the two sides do not agree on meat inspection rules. The EU has delisted U.S. slaughter plants and the United States has refused to accept EU poultry products.
"Yes, I would sy we have moved it (the issue) forward some," Glickman told reporters, but "We have not changed the (overall meat inspection) agreement."
Paul Drazek, trade adviser to Glickman, said USDA wanted to get a greater understanding of EU slaughter and inspection methods.
A 'veterinary equivalency' agreement between the two sides on inspection of red meats goes into effect this fall.
Another USDA official said no time was set for the team to assess the EU system.

During a 75-minute meeting before lunching together, Glickman and Fischler discussed several significant issues -- biotech crops and labeling rules for them, beef produced with use of synthetic growth hormones, a wine agreement that would spell out nomenclature for vinters and access for U.S. rice to the EU market.
"We talked in great detail on the GMO (genetically modified organism) issue," Glickman said.
"Hormone beef" was discussed briefly in the context of European consumer skepticism of biotech foods. Fischler and Glickman cited the need for more consumer education.
"We had a long list of issues to discuss," Fischler said. "We are making progress...We are solving problems."
Glickman also described the meeting as cordial and helpful although few concrete results were reached.
